proposals.spec_says: FR-004: All allocations are 4 KiB-aligned for NVMe DMA compatibility; FR-031: the reserve is whole pages at the top of the pool
proposals.code_does: reserve start = pool_ptr + (pool_size - reserve). That is 4 KiB-aligned only if pool_size % 4096 == 0, which initialize does not require. Example: pool_size=64*4096+100 gives cache_size=229476, so every lease is misaligned by 100 bytes, and the dispatcher DMAs device reads into leases
proposals.code_change: In initialize, round cache_size down to a page: `let cache_size = (pool_size - reserve) & !4095;` (the reserve then starts page-aligned; the sub-page tail, pool_size % 4096 bytes, is left unused by both and still counted in pool_info). Alternative: reject `pool_size % 4096 != 0` with InvalidSize. Add a test `a_reserve_in_an_unaligned_pool_is_page_aligned` (initialize(64*4096+100), pretend_dma, assert lease.ptr as usize % 4096 == 0); it fails on the current code.

spec_edits.old: | FR-031 | `initialize` sets aside a bounce reserve of `min(requested, pool_size / 8)` whole pages at the top of the pool (default
spec_edits.new: | FR-031 | `initialize` sets aside a bounce reserve of `min(requested, pool_size / 8)` whole pages, starting on a 4 KiB boundary, at the top of the pool (default

proposals.decision_point: Round cache_size down (keeps accepting any pool_size) or reject unaligned pool_size (changes US3 acceptance; a breaking error for raw-byte --memory-tier-size). Recommended: round down.

proposals.spec_says: The pool is held as a single, unsharded structure guarded by one `RwLock<Pool>`: a single first-fit free-list allocator and a single `HashMap<CacheKey, Slot>` slot map.
proposals.code_does: the cache is the pool less a bounce reserve with its own allocator

edits.old: Eviction decisions are delegated to an external `IEvictionPolicy` component via a receptacle binding, which provides pluggable eviction strategies (currently LRU) and its own internal synchronization; eviction-order touches are performed after releasing the pool lock.
edits.new: Eviction decisions are delegated to an external `IEvictionPolicy` component via a receptacle binding, which provides pluggable eviction strategies (currently LRU) and its own internal synchronization; eviction-order touches are performed after releasing the pool lock. The top of the pool (by default 16 MiB, at most an eighth) is a bounce reserve outside the cache, with its own allocator behind a mutex, leased to serve block-tier entries to peers (User Story 8); `capacity()`, `used()`, eviction and `clear()` cover only the cache.

proposals.spec_says: immutable state fields (`pool_ptr`, `pool_size`, `pool_id`); all mutable access is serialized through the `RwLock<Pool>`
proposals.code_does: cache_size is also immutable after init; the reserve is serialized by Mutex<Bounce>; leased bytes are owned by the lease holder

edits.old: After initialization the immutable state fields (`pool_ptr`, `pool_size`, `pool_id`) do not change;
edits.new: After initialization the immutable state fields (`pool_ptr`, `pool_size`, `cache_size`, `pool_id`) do not change;

edits.old: and all mutable access is serialized through the `RwLock<Pool>`.
edits.new: and all mutable allocator state is serialized: the cache's through the `RwLock<Pool>`, the bounce reserve's through `Mutex<Bounce>`; the bytes of a lease belong to its holder until `bounce_free`.

edits.old: // RwLock<Pool> serializes access. Immutable fields (pool_ptr, pool_size, spdk_allocated)
edits.new: // RwLock<Pool> and Mutex<Bounce> serialize access. Immutable fields (pool_ptr, pool_size, cache_size, spdk_allocated)

options.A: Keep it (current). Document in FR-031: 'the reserve is taken whether or not the pool is DMA-capable'. Simple; capacity is independent of the SPDK env.
